course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
title: External processors and trust boundaries
goal: Make an admission decision without executing an unknown external processor.

prerequisites.text: onec.p8; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.

sections.title: A format is not trust
paragraphs: An external processor is a program component, not a safe table simply because a menu opens it. Specify inputs, modified objects, files, network and output. Use original teaching source. Unknown emailed code must not run on the main computer merely for inspection.

EPF is executable processing and ERF may contain report code. A training filename or screenshot establishes no trust. Use a fictional unknown.epf card, not an actual unknown program: unknown source, known hash, no reviewed source code.

sections.title: Reconcile the complete experiment
paragraphs: A justified refusal is the observable result for this exercise.

code.source:
Card:unknown.epf; unknown origin; known SHA; no source.
Decision:NOT RUN. Alternative:own internal report.
code.output: Unknown file unopened; rejection reason and safe alternative recorded.

sections.title: Bind review to exact bytes
paragraphs: Source review, hash and version form provenance. Changed bytes need new review. Signatures and trusted sources help establish origin but do not replace authority analysis. Embed no secrets and collect no real diagnostic data; synthetic inputs should reproduce the issue.

SHA establishes byte identity, not safety. Record origin, distribution rights, source/dependencies, platform version, required privileges and file/network effects. Missing required information leaves the file NOT RUN.

sections.title: Safe mode has scope
paragraphs: Safe mode constrains specific capabilities in supported contexts; it does not prove full isolation of arbitrary configurations or the host. Rights, server security profiles andVMsare distinct. Choose an execution boundary for the actual threat and test denied actions in a permitted isolated stand.

An infobase copy protects original training data but the 1C process retains OS-user privileges. It is insufficient isolation for untrusted code. Optional engineering Sandbox also does not replace review or licensing.

sections.title: A case that distinguishes the wrong solution
paragraphs: Byte identity and data isolation address different questions.

code.source: Approve solely because the SHA matches or an infobase copy exists.

sections.title: Verification must not introduce risk
paragraphs: Inspect source without execution first. After admission, run a new synthetic copy under limits and reconcile effects. Test secret isolation with a synthetic canary, not real secrets. If isolation is unavailable, recordNOTRUN; successfulBSLLSanalysis is not execution.

Use the own internal report instead. For an own EPF retain reviewed source and test only admitted code in a separate copy, recording exact admission and actual execution. This does not authorize arbitrary external processors.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: A displayed number is accepted without its source. Reconcile actual references, units and raw values before presentation.
An unavailable feature is described as already tested. Record the exact edition and leave unperformed checks explicitly pending.
Hash identity is mistaken for safety or authorship. Separate byte integrity, reviewed trust and learner contribution.
